notes: One-time generated audio for Solmere. `music` beds are picked by the camera's zone + time of day + active world event and crossfaded slowly. `ambience` loops are spatial: placed at locations or spread over a district zone, gated by time-of-day windows and world events, low-passed with distance. `murmur` clips are short indistinct voices used for the conversation 'bumble' layer. Pipeline: `pnpm gen:audio` calls ElevenLabs and caches raw renders in .audio-cache/raw/ (never re-spent), then `pnpm master:audio` uses ffmpeg to pick a dynamically stable interior window of each music render, crossfade the loop seam, loudness-normalise to the per-group targets in `mastering`, downmix/encode, and write apps/web/public/audio/<id>.mp3 + manifest.json + master-report.json. Times are sim hours [start, end) and may wrap past midnight.

mix.listenerHeightCurve: above 90 m the camera hears a wide town mix; below 30 m it hears the local zone strongly

mastering.note: Two-pass ffmpeg loudnorm measurement, single linear gain applied (dynamic normalisation would re-introduce wandering loudness and smear the loop seam). Music sits well under the world; ambience a little louder; one-shots punch through; murmur stays quiet. limitHeadroomDb in master-audio.ts says how much peak limiting each group tolerates when linear gain alone cannot reach the target. seamCrossfade is the overlap-add length used to make loops seamless.
